sentences.n: وعظّم الله أجرك is the standard Muslim condolence, a wish: “may God enlarge your reward” (for bearing the loss). Note that the servants speak of Zubayda as “our mistress”.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا سَمِعَ ذَلِكَ يَبْكِي وَيَعِزُّ عَلَيْهِ فَإِنَّهُ يَعْمَلُ لَهَا الْخُتُومَاتِ وَيَسْهَرُ عَلَى قَبْرِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-idhā samiʿa dhālika yabkī wa-yaʿizzu ʿalayhi fa-innahu yaʿmalu lahā al-khutūmāti wa-yashharu ʿalā qabrihā
sentences.l: And-when he-hears that, he-weeps and-it-is-dear/hard upon-him, and-he will-make for-her the-completions and-keep-vigil over her-grave.
sentences.i: When he hears that, he will weep and be sorely grieved, and he will have the Qurʾān recited through for her and keep vigil at her grave.
sentences.n: عزّ عليه (ʿazza ʿalayhi) is “it is hard on him, it grieves him”. الختومات are khatmas, complete recitations of the Qurʾān held for the dead.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ قَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ إِنَّ بِنْتَ عَمِّي زُبَيْدَةَ مِنْ غِيرَتِهَا سَعَتْ فِي هَلَاكِ قُوتِ الْقُلُوبِ أَوْ غَلَبَ عَلَيْهِ الْهُيَامُ فَيَأْمُرُ بِإِخْرَاجِهَا مِنَ الْقَبْرِ فَلَا تَفْزَعِي مِنْ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-in qāla fī nafsihi inna binta ʿammī Zubaydata min ghīratihā saʿat fī halāki Qūti al-Qulūbi aw ghalaba ʿalayhi al-huyāmu fa-yaʾmuru bi-ikhrājihā mina al-qabri fa-lā tafzaʿī min dhālika
sentences.l: And-if he-says within-himself: Verily the-daughter-of my-paternal-uncle Zubayda, from her-jealousy, strove in the-destruction of-Qūt al-Qulūb, or overcame upon-him the-frenzy, then-he-commands the-bringing-out of-her from the-grave: then do-not be-alarmed at that.
sentences.i: And if he tells himself that his cousin Zubayda, out of jealousy, worked Qūt al-Qulūb's destruction, or if frenzied passion overmasters him, he may order her taken out of the grave. Do not be alarmed at that.
sentences.n: بنت عمي (“daughter of my paternal uncle”) is the Arabic for a cousin on the father's side; Zubayda was the caliph's cousin as well as his wife. الهيام (al-hiyām) is the madness of love, a passion that unseats reason.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا يَحْفِرُونَ وَيَطْلُعُونَ عَلَى تِلْكَ الصُّورَةِ الَّتِي كَبَنِي آدَمَ فَيَرَاهَا وَهِيَ مُكَفَّنَةٌ بِالْأَكْفَانِ الْمُفْتَخِرَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā yaḥfirūna wa-yaṭlaʿūna ʿalā tilka al-ṣūrati allatī ka-banī ādama fa-yarāhā wa-hiya mukaffanatun bi-al-akfāni al-muftakhirati
sentences.l: And-when they-dig and-come-upon that the-figure which is-like the-sons-of Adam, and-he-sees-it, and-it shrouded in-the-shrouds the-splendid-ones,
sentences.i: When they dig and come upon that figure, made in the likeness of a human being, he will see it wrapped in costly shrouds,
sentences.n: فلما يحفرون is لمّا followed by the imperfect, “when they dig”, a Middle Arabic pattern in place of the Classical perfect. المفتخرة (literally “boasting, proud”) is used for “splendid”; Classical would say الفاخرة.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ أَرَادَ الْخَلِيفَةُ إِزَالَةَ الْأَكْفَانِ عَنْهَا لِيَنْظُرَهَا فَامْنَعِيهِ أَنْتِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَالْأُخْرَى تَمْنَعُهُ وَتَقُولُ لَهُ رُؤْيَةُ عَوْرَتِهَا حَرَامٌ
sentences.tr: fa-in arāda al-khalīfatu izālata al-akfāni ʿanhā li-yanẓurahā fa-imnaʿīhi anti min dhālika wa-al-ukhrā tamnaʿuhu wa-taqūlu lahu ruʾyatu ʿawratihā ḥarāmun
sentences.l: And-if wants the-caliph the-removal of-the-shrouds from-her in-order-that-he-look-at-her, then-prevent-him, you, from that, and-the-other prevents-him and-says to-him: The-seeing of-her nakedness is forbidden.
sentences.i: And if the caliph wants to strip the shrouds from her to look at her, you must stop him; and the other woman will hold him back too, telling him that to see her nakedness is forbidden.
sentences.n: والأخرى (“and the other [woman]”) is not clear. The old woman is the one who later says “put her back”, so I take her to mean herself, speaking of herself at one remove; she may also mean a second attendant. عورة (ʿawra) is whatever must be kept covered, the private parts.

sentences.t: فَيُصَدِّقُ حِينَئِذٍ أَنَّهَا مَاتَتْ فَيُعِيدُهَا إِلَى مَكَانِهَا وَيَشْكُرُكِ عَلَى فِعْلِكِ وَتَخْلُصِينَ أَنْتِ إِنْ شَاءَاللَّهُ تَعَالَى مِنْ هَذِهِ الْوَرْطَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-yuṣaddiqu ḥīnaʾidhin annahā mātat fa-yuʿīduhā ilā makānihā wa-yashkuruki ʿalā fiʿlika wa-takhluṣīna anti in shāʾa Allāhu taʿālā min hādhihi al-warṭati
sentences.l: And-he-believes then that she died, and-returns-her to her-place, and-thanks-you for your-deed, and-you-escape, you, if God-wills, the-Exalted, from this the-predicament.
sentences.i: Then he will believe that she is dead, put her back in her place and thank you for what you did, and you, God willing, will be out of this predicament.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتِ السِّتُّ زُبَيْدَةُ كَلَامَهَا رَأَتْهُ صَوَابًا فَخَلَعَتْ عَلَيْهَا خِلْعَةً وَأَمَرَتْهَا أَنْ تَفْعَلَ ذَلِكَ بَعْدَ مَا أَعْطَتْهَا جُمْلَةً مِنَ الْمَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿati al-sittu Zubaydatu kalāmahā raʾathu ṣawāban fa-khalaʿat ʿalayhā khilʿatan wa-amarathā an tafʿala dhālika baʿda mā aʿṭathā jumlatan mina al-māli
sentences.l: And-when heard the-lady Zubayda her-speech, she-saw-it right, and-she-bestowed upon-her a-robe-of-honour, and-commanded-her that she-do that, after she-gave-her a-sum of the-money.
sentences.i: When Lady Zubayda heard her words she judged them sound, and she bestowed a robe of honour on her, gave her a good sum of money, and bade her carry out the plan.
sentences.n: خلع عليها خلعة, “she bestowed a robe on her”, is the formal gesture of favour. The sum is given before the order is carried out.

sentences.t: فَشَرَعَتِ الْعَجُوزُ فِى الْحَالِ وَأَمَرَتِ النَّجَّارَ أَنْ يَعْمَلَ لَهَا صُورَةً كَمَا ذَكَرْنَا
sentences.tr: fa-sharaʿati al-ʿajūzu fī al-ḥāli wa-amarati al-najjāra an yaʿmala lahā ṣūratan ka-mā dhakarnā
sentences.l: And-began the-old-woman at the-moment, and-commanded the-carpenter that he-make for-her a-figure, as we-mentioned.
sentences.i: The old woman set about it at once and ordered a carpenter to make the figure as described above.
sentences.n: كما ذكرنا (“as we mentioned”) is the narrator's “we”, Shahrazād referring back to the old woman's instructions.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ تَمَامِ الصُّورَةِ جَاءَتْ بِهَا إِلَى السِّتِّ زُبَيْدَةَ فَكَفَّنَتْهَا وَدَفَنَتْهَا وَأَوْقَدَتِ الشُّمُوعَ وَالْقَنَادِيلَ وَفَرَشَتِ الْبُسُطَ حَوْلَ الْقَبْرِ وَلَبِسَتِ السَّوَادَ وَأَمَرَتِ الْجَوَارِيَ أَنْ يَلْبَسْنَ السَّوَادَ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda tamāmi al-ṣūrati jāʾat bihā ilā al-sitti Zubaydata fa-kaffanathā wa-dafanathā wa-awqadati al-shumūʿa wa-al-qanādīla wa-farashati al-busuṭa ḥawla al-qabri wa-labisati al-sawāda wa-amarati al-jawāriya an yalbasna al-sawāda
sentences.l: And-after the-completion of-the-figure, she-came with-it to the-lady Zubayda, and-she-shrouded-it and-buried-it, and-lit the-candles and-the-lamps, and-spread the-carpets around the-grave, and-put-on the-black, and-commanded the-slave-girls that they-put-on the-black.
sentences.i: When the figure was finished, the old woman brought it to Lady Zubayda, who shrouded it and buried it, lit the candles and lamps, spread carpets around the grave, put on black, and ordered her slave girls to do the same.
sentences.n: Every verb here is feminine singular, so the print does not mark the change of subject. I take the old woman as the subject of “she came with it” and Zubayda as the subject of the rest, since it is Zubayda who wears black and commands the slave girls.

sentences.t: وَاشْتَهَرَ الْأَمْرُ فِى الْقَصْرَانِ قُوتُ الْقُلُوبِ مَاتَتْ
sentences.tr: wa-ishtahara al-amru fī al-qaṣrāni Qūtu al-Qulūbi mātat
sentences.l: And-became-widely-known the-matter in the-two-palaces: Qūt al-Qulūb has-died.
sentences.i: And word went round both palaces: Qūt al-Qulūb is dead.

sentences.t: فَبَعْدَ مُدَّةٍ أَقْبَلَ الْخَلِيفَةُ مِنْ غَيْبَتِهِ وَطَلَعَ إِلَى قَصْرِهِ وَلَكِنْ مَالَهُ شُغْلٌ إِلَّا قُوتُ الْقُلُوبِ
sentences.tr: fa-baʿda muddatin aqbala al-khalīfatu min ghaybatihi wa-ṭalaʿa ilā qaṣrihi wa-lākin mālahu shughlun illā Qūtu al-Qulūbi
sentences.l: And-after a-while advanced the-caliph from his-absence, and-went-up to his-palace, but there-was-not to-him an-occupation except Qūt al-Qulūb.
sentences.i: After a while the caliph came back from his absence and went up to his palace, though he had no thought for anything but Qūt al-Qulūb.
sentences.n: The print writes ماله as one word. ما له شغل إلا X is “he has no business but X”, the idiom for being wholly preoccupied.

sentences.t: فَرَأَى الْغِلْمَانَ وَالْخُدَّامَ وَالْجَوَارِيَ كُلَّهُمْ لَابِسِينَ السَّوَادَ فَرَجَفَ فُؤَادُ الْخَلِيفَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-raʾā al-ghilmāna wa-al-khuddāma wa-al-jawāriya kullahum lābisīna al-sawāda fa-rajafa fuʾādu al-khalīfati
sentences.l: And-he-saw the-boys and-the-servants and-the-slave-girls, all-of-them wearing the-black, and-quaked the-heart of-the-caliph.
sentences.i: He saw the pages, the servants and the slave girls, every one of them dressed in black, and the caliph's heart shook within him.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ الْقَصْرَ عَلَى السِّتِّ زُبَيْدَةَ رَآهَا لَابِسَةً لِلسَّوَادِ فَسَأَلَ الْخَلِيفَةُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَأَخْبَرُوهُ بِمَوْتِ قُوتِ الْقُلُوبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhala al-qaṣra ʿalā al-sitti Zubaydata raʾāhā lābisatan li-al-sawādi fa-saʾala al-khalīfatu ʿan dhālika fa-akhbarūhu bi-mawti Qūti al-Qulūbi
sentences.l: And-when he-entered the-palace upon the-lady Zubayda, he-saw-her wearing for-the-black, and-asked the-caliph about that, and-they-informed-him of-the-death of-Qūt al-Qulūb.
sentences.i: When he went into the palace to Lady Zubayda and saw her dressed in black, the caliph asked the reason, and they told him of Qūt al-Qulūb's death.
sentences.n: لابسة للسواد: لابس normally takes its object directly (لابسةً السوادَ, as in the previous sentence); here the object is introduced by a pleonastic لـ, a common Middle Arabic habit.

sentences.t: فَوَقَعَ مُغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَ سَأَلَ عَنْ قَبْرِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-waqaʿa mughshiyyan ʿalayhi fa-lammā afāqa saʾala ʿan qabrihā
sentences.l: And-he-fell overcome-with-swoon upon-him; and-when he-recovered he-asked about her-grave.
sentences.i: He fell down in a swoon, and when he came to himself he asked where her grave was.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ السِّتُّ زُبَيْدَةُ اعْلَمْ يَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنَّنِي مِنْ مَعَزَّتِهَا عِنْدِي دَفَنْتُهَا فِي قَصْرِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-sittu Zubaydatu iʿlam yā amīra al-muʾminīna annanī min maʿazzatihā ʿindī dafantuhā fī qaṣrī
sentences.l: And-said the-lady Zubayda: Know, O commander of-the-believers, that-I, from her-dearness with-me, buried-her in my-palace.
sentences.i: Lady Zubayda said: Know, Commander of the Faithful, that she was so dear to me that I buried her in my own palace.
sentences.n: The print writes اميرالمؤمنين as one word. من معزتها عندي is “from (= because of) her dearness to me”.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ الْخَلِيفَةُ بِثِيَابِ السَّفَرِ إِلَى قَبْرِ قُوتِ الْقُلُوبِ لِيَزُورَهَا فَوَجَدَ الْبُسُطَ مَفْرُوشَةً وَالشُّمُوعَ وَالْقَنَادِيلَ مَوْقُودَةً
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala al-khalīfatu bi-thiyābi al-safari ilā qabri Qūti al-Qulūbi li-yazūrahā fa-wajada al-busuṭa mafrūshatan wa-al-shumūʿa wa-al-qanādīla mawqūdatan
sentences.l: And-entered the-caliph in-the-clothes of-the-journey to the-grave of-Qūt al-Qulūb in-order-to-visit-her, and-found the-carpets spread and-the-candles and-the-lamps lit.
sentences.i: So the caliph went, still in his travelling clothes, to the grave of Qūt al-Qulūb to visit her, and found the carpets spread and the candles and lamps burning.
sentences.n: موقودة is feminine singular for a plural of things, as Arabic regularly does with inanimates.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآى ذَلِكَ شَكَرَهَا عَلَى فِعْلِهَا فَبَقِيَ حَائِرًا فِي أَمْرِةِ وَهُوَ مَا بَيْنَ مُصَدِّقٍ وَمُكَذِّبٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā dhālika shakarahā ʿalā fiʿlihā fa-baqiya ḥāʾiran fī amrihi wa-huwa mā bayna muṣaddiqin wa-mukadhdhibin
sentences.l: And-when he-saw that, he-thanked-her for her-deed, and-remained perplexed in his-affair, and-he between a-believer and-a-disbeliever.
sentences.i: When he saw this he thanked her for what she had done, yet he stayed perplexed about the matter, torn between belief and disbelief.
sentences.n: امرة is printed with ة (tāʾ marbūṭa); a misprint for امره (amrihi, “his affair”) is almost certain, and that is how it is read. ما بين: the ما is only a filler before بين.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا غَلَبَ عَلَيْهِ الْوَسْوَاسُ أَمَرَ بِحَفْرِ الْقَبْرِ وَأَخْرَجَهَا مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ghalaba ʿalayhi al-waswāsu amara bi-ḥafri al-qabri wa-akhrajahā minhu
sentences.l: And-when overcame upon-him the-whispering-of-doubt, he-commanded the-digging of-the-grave, and-brought-her-out from-it.
sentences.i: But when doubt got the better of him, he ordered the grave dug up and her brought out of it.
sentences.n: الوسواس (al-waswās) is the insidious inner whispering, here a nagging doubt; it is also the word for the devil's prompting.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآى الْكَفَنَ وَأَرَادَأَنْ يُزِيلَهُ عَنْهَا لِيَرَاهَا خَافَ مِنَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā al-kafana wa-arāda an yuzīlahu ʿanhā li-yarāhā khāfa mina Allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: And-when he-saw the-shroud and-wanted that he-remove-it from-her in-order-to-see-her, he-feared from God the-Exalted.
sentences.i: But when he saw the shroud and was about to remove it from her to look at her, he feared God Most High.
sentences.n: The print runs وأراد and أن together (وارادان). خاف من is “to fear”, with the person or power feared introduced by من.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْعَجُوزُ رُدُّوهَا إِلَى مَكَانِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-ʿajūzu ruddūhā ilā makānihā
sentences.l: And-said the-old-woman: Return-her to her-place.
sentences.i: Then the old woman said: Put her back where she was.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ أَمَرَ فِى الْحَالِ بِإِحْضَارِ الْفُقَهَاءِ وَالْمُقْرِئِينَ وَعَمِلَ الْخُتُومَاتِ عَلَى قَبْرِهَا وَجَلَسَ بِجَانِبِ الْقَبْرِ يَبْكِي إِلَى أَنْ غُشِيَ عَلَيْهِ وَلَمْ يَزَلْ قَاعِدًا عَلَى قَبْرِهَا شَهْرًا كَامِلًا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-khalīfata amara fī al-ḥāli bi-iḥḍāri al-fuqahāʾi wa-al-muqriʾīna wa-ʿamila al-khutūmāti ʿalā qabrihā wa-jalasa bi-jānibi al-qabri yabkī ilā an ghushiya ʿalayhi wa-lam yazal qāʿidan ʿalā qabrihā shahran kāmilan
sentences.l: Then, verily the-caliph commanded at-once the-bringing-present of-the-jurists and-the-reciters, and-made the-completions over her-grave, and-sat beside the-grave weeping until he-was-swooned upon, and-did-not cease sitting upon her-grave a-month complete.
sentences.i: Then the caliph at once ordered the jurists and Qurʾān reciters to be summoned, and had the Qurʾān recited through at her grave. He sat beside the tomb weeping until he swooned, and he kept his seat at her grave for a whole month.
sentences.n: الفقهاء are the scholars of religious law; المقرئين the professional Qurʾān reciters.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَ—احِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And-overtook Shahrazād the-morning, and-she-fell-silent from the-speech the-permitted.
sentences.i: Then morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, breaking off her permitted speech.
sentences.n: The night-ending formula. The dash inside المب—اح is a printing artefact; the word is المباح, “the permitted”, as in the stock phrase for the speech Shahrazād is allowed to utter.
